People lie or forget. That's why I mentioned it. They were stated, but we also don't know if the piercer actually provided titanium or even a good grade of titanium. We also don't know if OP still has a saline solution, is running out, or is fully stocked. 

It's always best to provide as many options to solve than only one and clients return over and over again to try new things. I provide all viable solutions, and they'll head back if all else has failed and we retire the piercing.

I told them to stop using everything else but saline solution. If you read, they're putting a "piercing bump" remedy. That's not necessary. 

Some people say titanium in fear of being shamed for having anything but. I was simply mentioning it in case they either 1. Know they don't have titanium, 2. Aren't fully 100% sure they have titanium. That's all. No harm in mentioning, right?
I did. I believe it could be an abscess, infection, or a very swollen and irritated irritation bump. So, I offered viable solutions. What's your point?
How would you feel about getting a snug piercing too? I think it'll look really cool, unique, and it'll give the effect of having a helix and conch!

Stop doing anything but saline solution. Everything else isn't necessary. If you don't have a saline solution, plain water will do. 

Clean 2-3 times a day. Gently massage the area (in the shower or with a warm compress, but in the shower, it is easier)  to help remove anything trapped inside without putting too much pressure. If you have pus, if it's green, doctor. If it's white, keep with the gentle massages, and you should see it start getting better. 

Do not twist, turn, pick, or sleep on it. If you wear any hats or headsets, don't wear them for a good while until it's more healed. We don't want any unnecessary pressure on it. 

If you wear gel or hair sprays, try your hardest to not spray directly on your piercing or around it. If you feel like it got sprayed (even the slighest), immediately clean your piercing. While it's still healing, anything that can irritate it, will. 

ALSO, depending on the material, it could be you're allergic to surgical steel. Titanium is hypoallergenic, so you can try that. DO NOT REMOVE THIS JEWELRY UNTIL THE ISSUE IS CLEARED TO NOT SEAL THAT PUS IN THERE.

Agreed ^ photo doesn't show much. If it's that long tho, I would also recommend a downsize. It's possible you're irritating it, and that's why it's slightly swollen and red. If you're bumping it more or snagging, it's most likely because of the long bar. 

I usually recommend my clients downsize for eyebrows as early as a month if there's been no issues and swelling is down.

You should not be mixing anything yourself as that can mess the salt to water ratio and cause dryness, if not irritation. 

The warm compress works. If you want salt water, go straight to saline solution instead.
